q: What are the terms of SIDBI's Green Finance Scheme loan for MSMEs?
title: SIDBI Green Finance Scheme loan terms
short: SIDBI's Green Finance Scheme is a term loan, in rupees or foreign currency, for solar, energy efficiency, compressed biogas, water, waste and e-mobility projects. It funds up to 75 percent of project cost, capped at ₹100 crore, with repayment set to the project. New and existing Udyam-registered MSMEs can apply.
audience: MSME owners and finance heads planning a solar, efficiency or effluent project

ul: Renewable energy, such as rooftop or ground-mounted solar.
Water and wastewater management, including effluent treatment.
Solid waste management, resource efficiency and cleaner production.

sections.h: How much, and for how long
ul: Up to 75 percent of total project cost, so plan to fund at least a quarter yourself.
Maximum loan ₹100 crore, for an MSME or for a service provider or aggregator with an established MSME linkage.
Repayment tenure set to the project's needs, rather than a fixed number of years.
Rupee or foreign currency term loan, with fixed or floating rate options.
The loan may be covered under risk sharing facilities such as CGTMSE or PRSF.

p: Older write-ups of this scheme describe 100 percent financing, a ₹20 crore cap for an MSME and ten-year repayment. SIDBI's page now shows 75 percent, ₹100 crore and a tenure set per project. The practical change for a small unit is the 25 percent: line up that money, from reserves or a separate facility, before you sign the solar or effluent contract.

New and existing MSMEs with valid Udyam registration, a satisfactory credit history and no defaults to any bank or financial institution. Installers and service companies on the supply side, such as RESCOs, ESCOs, EPC contractors and vendors, can also apply. Every borrower must comply with SIDBI's Environment and Social Management Framework.

ul: Use GFS for solar, effluent, biogas, waste or e-mobility projects, for a new unit, or above ₹15 crore.
Look at 4E for a pure efficiency retrofit in a unit with three years of cash profit: it can fund 100 percent against a 25 percent fixed deposit, repaid over up to 84 months.
Neither page states an interest rate. Get the rate and security in the sanction letter before you place an equipment order.

example.title: A dyeing unit adds 300 kW of solar and water recycling
lines: Solar output: 300 kW x 1,400 kWh per kW a year (assumed yield) = 4,20,000 kWh
CO2 avoided: 4,20,000 kWh x 0.675 kg per kWh (CEA grid factor, FY 2025-26) = 2,83,500 kg, about 283 tonnes a year
example.note: Use your installer's site estimate for yield. The CO2 figure only holds if the solar units replace grid units you were buying, which your bills before and after will show.

senseible: Senseible turns your electricity bills and fuel invoices into a dated baseline and a before and after record of the project, the evidence a green loan appraisal and later reporting ask for. SIDBI decides the loan.
